vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Fixes for a known vulnerability are proposed at once (no minimumReleaseAge) and merge themselves once ci-ok passes.

helm-values.description: Chart images are digest-pinned, so the customManager below owns them. helm-values cannot update a digest; it would move the tag and leave the digest stale.

customManagers.description: Digest-pinned images in the chart and the e2e harness. The forms are `<repo/name>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>`, or the keys `repository:`, `tag:` and `digest:` in that order (comment lines may sit between them), or `repository:` then `tag: <tag>@sha256:<digest>`. Official images need a namespace, as in `docker.io/library/<name>`. test/e2e YAML and Go are scanned because ignorePaths above replaces the preset list, which skips **/test/**: the e2e harness pulls these images too. The workflows are scanned for the images their steps pin (setup-qemu-action's binfmt image); their `uses:` actions stay the github-actions manager's. Dockerfiles are left to the dockerfile manager, so no image is extracted twice.

packageRules.description: Wait 3 days after a release before proposing it, so a bad release can be yanked first.
Images wait 3 days too, a re-pushed tag (a new digest) as much as a new tag. A registry that gives no timestamp (gcr.io's distroless) is not held back for ever.

prBodyNotes: Keep the k8s.io minor in step with nixpkgs' `kubernetes` (envtest's kube-apiserver; see flake.nix). A new minor here usually needs a flake.lock bump too.

packageRules.description: The Go minor comes from the flake (go_1_26 and GOTOOLCHAIN=local). The builder image follows patches only; a new Go minor changes flake.nix and the Dockerfile together, by hand.
andrius/asterisk tags look like 22.11.0_debian-trixie. The suffix must match exactly, so -amd64 and -<sha> variants are never proposed.
Stay on Asterisk 22 LTS. Moving to the next LTS is a design change, not a bump.
Not Renovate's to move: our own images (released by CI: patchbay and the stream bridge), and kind node images (they must match the kind from the flake).
tonistiigi/binfmt (CI's QEMU, for the stream bridge's arm64 build) tags look like qemu-v10.2.3: only those are proposed.

Alpine is the stream bridge's base, for its ffmpeg (docs/plans/release-b.md §2(f)). Its updates, digests and minors, merge themselves once ci-ok passes like every non-major image: the bridge holds no credentials (unlike Asterisk), the image job checks its ffmpeg (test/image), and e2e plays through it. A new Alpine minor is a new ffmpeg.

A major update waits for a human. Everything else (but Asterisk, below) merges itself once ci-ok (check, e2e, image) passes: GitHub does the merge (platformAutomerge), so the main ruleset decides what passing means (docs/releasing.md).

The Asterisk image never merges itself, digest updates included: andrius/asterisk is a community image that runs on the PBX node's host network and reads every SIP password and the AMI secret, and CI tests behaviour, not provenance. A person reads the upstream change and the new digest (one that changes behind an unchanged tag is the signal) before it can reach a release.
